newsitem.title: USA: INTELSAT board approves tariff reductions, pricing.
newsitem.headline: INTELSAT board approves tariff reductions, pricing.

text.p: INTELSAT said Wednesday that its board of governors had approved a package of tariff reductions and substantive revisions to its voice/data service pricing structure.
The company said in a statement Wednesday evening that the changes will result in long-term discounts, more uniform pricing and more long-term capacity commitments.
It did not provide details of the pricing changes, and no one at the company's offices in Washington, D.C. was immediately available to provide more information.

INTELSAT, which owns and operates the world's most extensive global communications satellite system, also said its board had extended the term of its chief executive, Irving Goldstein, by eight months, from February 1988 to October 1988.
